$comment: Measured topology of the HyperCube Nano. Derived from observation, not documentation - the vendor publishes none of this and its own numbers disagree with the controller's.

device.deadAddresses: 44-87 - configured but no physical tap exists
device.$comment: Identifiers omitted deliberately; this describes the product, not one unit.

topology.$comment: One data line enters on a vertical edge and splits at corners. Every edge downstream of a split carries the same signal, so those edges always show identical colour. Fan-out is UNEVEN, which is why no single 'LEDs per address' figure exists.

consequences: Edges within a block are electrically ganged and cannot differ in colour.
Position along an edge IS controllable - address k of a block maps to position k on every edge that block drives.
A single point cannot traverse the cube's perimeter; it appears on 1, 2, 4 or 5 edges depending on which block it is in.
Radial, symmetric and blooming patterns suit this hardware. Per-edge independent control does not.
openQuestions: Exact identity of each edge per block (which vertical, which top edge).
Direction of travel on each edge within a block - test 5 showed ends map to ends, but not which end is which.
Whether the 1/2/4/5 split is exact or whether block boundaries sit slightly off the 11-address grid.
